paras.en: It was now the eighth day since my plane had broken down in the desert, and I had listened to the merchant’s story as I drank the last drop of my water supply:
paras.zh: 我的飞机在沙漠里出了故障，到这时已经是第八天了。我一边听商贩的故事，一边喝完了储备的最后一滴水：

paras.en: “Ah!” I said to the little prince. “Those memories of yours are lovely, but I still haven’t repaired my plane, I have nothing left to drink, and I too would be happy if I could walk very slowly towards a fountain!”
paras.zh: “唉！”我对小王子说，“你的那些回忆真美，可我的飞机还没修好，也没有什么可喝的了。要是能慢慢地走向一眼泉水，我也会很高兴的！”

paras.en: “My friend the fox…” he said to me.
paras.zh: “我的狐狸朋友……”他对我说。

paras.en: “My little fellow, it’s not about the fox any more!”
paras.zh: “小家伙，现在不是说狐狸的时候了！”

paras.en: “Why?”
paras.zh: “为什么？”

paras.en: “Because we’re going to die of thirst…”
paras.zh: “因为我们就要渴死了……”

paras.en: He did not understand my reasoning. He replied:
paras.zh: 他不明白我的道理，回答我说：

paras.en: “It’s good to have had a friend, even if you’re going to die. I’m very glad to have had a fox for a friend…”
paras.zh: “曾经有过一个朋友，是件好事，哪怕就要死了。我呢，很高兴曾有一只狐狸做朋友……”

paras.en: He doesn’t realise the danger, I told myself. He is never hungry or thirsty. A little sunshine is enough for him…
paras.zh: 他不知道这有多危险，我心想。他从来不饿，也从来不渴。一点阳光就够他了……

paras.en: But he looked at me and answered my thought:
paras.zh: 可他看着我，回答了我心里的话：

paras.en: “I’m thirsty too... Let’s look for a well...”
paras.zh: “我也渴了……我们找一口井吧……”

paras.en: I made a weary gesture: it is absurd to look for a well at random in the vastness of the desert. Still, we set off walking.
paras.zh: 我做了个疲倦的手势：在茫茫沙漠里碰运气地找一口井，实在荒唐。可我们还是迈开了脚步。

paras.en: After we had walked for hours in silence, night fell, and the stars began to shine. I saw them as though in a dream, a little feverish from thirst. The little prince’s words danced in my memory:
paras.zh: 我们默默地走了好几个小时，夜幕降临，星星开始亮起来。我渴得有些发烧，看着那些星星，像在梦里一样。小王子的话在我的记忆里跳着舞：

paras.en: “So you’re thirsty too?” I asked him.
paras.zh: “这么说，你也渴了？”我问他。

paras.en: But he did not answer my question. He simply said to me:
paras.zh: 可他没有回答我的问题。他只是对我说：

paras.en: “Water can be good for the heart too...”
paras.zh: “水也能对心有好处……”

paras.en: I did not understand his answer, but I kept quiet... I knew very well that I should not question him.
paras.zh: 我没明白他的回答，却没有再说话……我很清楚，不该追问他。

paras.en: He was tired. He sat down. I sat down beside him. And, after a silence, he spoke again:
paras.zh: 他累了。他坐了下来。我在他身旁坐下。沉默了一会儿，他又说：

paras.en: “The stars are beautiful because of a flower we cannot see...”
paras.zh: “星星很美，因为有一朵看不见的花……”

paras.en: I answered, “Of course,” and looked, without speaking, at the folds of sand beneath the moon.
paras.zh: 我回答说“当然”，便默默地望着月光下沙地的褶皱。

paras.en: “The desert is beautiful,” he added...
paras.zh: “沙漠很美，”他又说……

paras.en: And it was true. I have always loved the desert. You sit down on a sand dune. You see nothing. You hear nothing. And yet something shines in silence...
paras.zh: 确实如此。我一直喜欢沙漠。你坐在沙丘上。什么也看不见。什么也听不见。然而，有什么在静静地发光……

paras.en: “What gives the desert its beauty,” said the little prince, “is that it hides a well somewhere...”
paras.zh: “让沙漠变美的，”小王子说，“是它在某个地方藏着一口井……”

paras.en: To my surprise, I suddenly understood that mysterious glow of the sand. When I was a little boy, I lived in an old house, and legend said that a treasure lay buried there. Of course, no one ever managed to find it, and perhaps no one had even looked for it. But it enchanted the whole house. My house hid a secret deep in its heart...
paras.zh: 我忽然明白了沙地那神秘的光芒，连自己都感到惊讶。我还是个小男孩的时候，住在一座老房子里，传说那里埋着一份宝藏。当然，从来没有人找到过它，也许甚至没人找过。可它让整座房子都带上了魔力。我的房子在内心深处藏着一个秘密……

paras.en: “Yes,” I said to the little prince, “whether it is the house, the stars or the desert, what gives them their beauty is invisible!”
paras.zh: “是啊，”我对小王子说，“无论是房子、星星，还是沙漠，让它们美丽的东西都是看不见的！”

paras.en: “I am glad,” he said, “that you agree with my fox.”
paras.zh: “你赞同我的狐狸，”他说，“我真高兴。”

paras.en: As the little prince was falling asleep, I took him in my arms and set off again. I was moved. It seemed to me that I was carrying a fragile treasure. It even seemed to me that nothing on Earth could be more fragile. In the moonlight, I looked at his pale forehead, his closed eyes, those strands of hair trembling in the wind, and I said to myself: “What I see here is only bark. What matters most is invisible...”
paras.zh: 小王子渐渐睡着了，我把他抱在怀里，重新上路。我心里很感动。我觉得自己仿佛抱着一份脆弱的宝藏。我甚至觉得，地球上再没有比他更脆弱的东西了。借着月光，我望着那苍白的额头，那闭着的双眼，那些在风里颤动的发丝，心想：“我眼前看到的，不过是一层树皮。最要紧的，是看不见的……”

paras.en: As his slightly parted lips began to form a half-smile, I said to myself again: “What moves me so deeply about this sleeping little prince is his faithfulness to a flower; it is the image of a rose shining within him like the flame of a lamp, even while he sleeps...” And I sensed that he was more fragile still. Lamps must be carefully protected: a gust of wind can put them out...
paras.zh: 他微微张开的嘴唇隐约露出一丝笑意，我又想：“这个睡着的小王子，让我如此感动的，是他对一朵花的忠诚，是一朵玫瑰的模样，像一盏灯的火苗，在他心里发光，哪怕他睡着了也一样……”于是我隐隐觉得，他还要更加脆弱。灯一定要好好护着：一阵风就能把它们吹灭……

paras.en: And as I walked on like this, I found the well at daybreak.
paras.zh: 就这样走着，天亮时，我找到了那口井。
